newsitem.title: UK: Mergers to continue in mining industry - Roskill.
newsitem.headline: Mergers to continue in mining industry - Roskill.

text.p: More than $14 billion was spent in mergers and acquisitions in the mining industry over the past year, and this "merger mania" is seen continuing, a study published by Roskill Information Services said.

Who owns Who in Mining, which was edited by the Raw Materials Group (RMG), said the spate of mergers that started in 1995 was checked only by the Busang/Bre-X Minerals Ltd gold scandal earlier in 1997.
"Although both the number of deals and the amount of capital have fallen since then, over $14 billion were still spent on mergers and acquisitions between June 1996 and May 1997," the study said.
The pace of mergers will continue throughout the rest of this year, although there will be a degree of long-term caution now.
This reflects caution following the Bre-X scandal and questions over whether all these deals really pay off for shareholders, RMG says.
Despite the Bre-X affair, mergers still account for more money in mining than outright exploration. Total annual world expenditure on exploration activities is around $4 billion only.
This is because mergers and takeovers avoid the costly, risky exploration phase of a mine project, which is increasingly the province of the junior companies.
Small companies tend to be more entrepreneurial and efficient in finding new ore bodies than a major company.
"However, when the deposit is located and shall be exploited there are no advantages, only disadvantages, in being a small company. And the project will be up for grabs," the study added.
South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd remains the world's largest mining company in RMG's top 50 list, which reflects the value of the mine production controlled by each firm.
In the rankings for 1995, the latest year for which data is available, Rio Tinto of the U.K. is second ahead of Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd of Australia.

Elsewhere in the top 10, ASARCO Inc has moved up to eigth from 13th, Inco Ltd has gained four places, coming in at number 10, while Phelps Dodge Corp has climbed three places to the number seven slot.
Notable fallers in the rankings include Sweden's Trelleborg AB, down from 29 to 46 due to its sale of its Falconbridge Ltd interests, and Barrick Gold Corp, down six to 14.
